records.n: John Chavis Memorial Park – Phase 2 Aquatic Center
records.description: This project proposes the construction of a new two-story aquatic center as part of Phase 2 of the John Chavis Memorial Park Master Plan. The Phase 2 Aquatic Center project, located alongside the existing John Chavis Community Center and the historic Allan Herschell Carousel, includes approximately five acres of site development and construction of a new indoor/outdoor aquatic facility and Heritage Plaza. The aquatic center will include approximately 25,000 SF of mixed-use interior space consisting of assembly areas, locker rooms, administrative offices, mechanical and equipment rooms, storage, and other support spaces. Indoor aquatic amenities include a 3,160 SF competition/lap pool and a 1,400 SF therapy pool. The outdoor aquatic area will encompass approximately 10,300 SF and feature a 4,600 SF activity pool with a lazy river, vortex, water recreation area, and a two-story waterslide. The building's architectural design is highlighted by an overhead oval-shaped perforated metal "crown" that distinguishes the facility's roofline and references the park's historic carousel. The project also includes reconfiguration of site parking, upgrades to the Heritage Plaza with a historically inspired public art installation, repairs to the existing stone bridge, and new connections to the South Park Heritage Trail. The aquatic center will be a fully sprinklered, steel-framed structure with mixed assembly and business occupancies. The scope of work includes complete civil, structural, architectural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, and site utility systems to provide a modern, year-round aquatic facility that honors the historic legacy of John Chavis Memorial Park while serving the recreational and community needs of future generations.

records.description: The Virginia IT Agency (VITA), on behalf of the Commonwealth of Virginia (Commonwealth), is seeking a supplier to deliver enterprise-wide, next generation End User Computing (EUC) Services to Virginia Executive Branch agencies and other public bodies. VITA is looking for a strategic partnership offering fully managed, secure, and compliant end-user services, while also providing flexibility to support management of both supplier-owned devices and Commonwealth-owned/leased devices. Additionally, VITA is also seeking supplier input on simplification of device offerings and other available transformative efforts that modernize the environment while containing costs. The Supplier will provide end-to-end service delivery, including device support, software support, troubleshooting, lifecycle management, and required financial and asset tracking processes (e.g., CMDB, GASB compliance) for all devices/workstations. Suppliers may propose value-added or premium services as optional capabilities available to agencies. During the life of the contract, Supplier will propose to VITA continual improvement of service/device offerings while meeting Customer needs and requirements, focusing on service quality, operational efficiency, and customer experience. The EUC supplier will be required to integrate as a full Tier 1supplier*. The EUC supplier may bring a suite of tools to manage the service platform, but all EUC provided tools shall not utilize proprietary tools or formats that hinder or prohibit integration into the MSI platform/VITA Toolkit. VITA and the MSI integrator shall have full, uninhibited real-time visibility into the content and configuration of all EUC provided tools.VITA anticipates a single award to one supplier for EUC services, while reserving the right to continually adjust the device ownership structure based on the best value and most suitable solution to the Commonwealth. VITA also reserves the right to issue a single award, multiple awards, or no award. While VITAs Managed Environment is comprised of various and separate scopes of services provided by multiple Integrated Suppliers (also called Service Tower Suppliers), the multi-provider model requires coordination, cooperation and integration among the Integrated Suppliers. These suppliers must work together toward the common goal of providing uninterrupted, high-quality services to VITA & the Commonwealth. In this regard, the participants must perform their services, interact, and cooperate with each other in a manner that, as a foremost guiding principle, first considers the best interests of VITA & the Commonwealth.
